item.title: Seeing pivotal election, Israelis fly from around world to vote
item.description:
Liran Naaman said he spent 800 euros (nearly $900) to fly from Amsterdam, where he has lived for the past 11 years, to his native Israel, all to vote in the October 27 election.

He has returned to vote in every election except during the Covid-19 pandemic, and believes this time his participation matters more than ever. "The way that our government is conducting itself is harming me personally and the rest of the Israelis abroad," the project manager told AFP.

item.title: Regulator 'will resign' if any political interference in Man City case
item.description:
The chair of English football's Independent Regulator has said he will resign if there is political interference in any future investigation into Manchester City as a result of widespread impropriety. 

City have been found guilty on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules by an independent commission.

The club have appealed and deny any wrongdoing, but face a severe sanction unless they overturn the verdict.

item.title: Iran shifting tactics to step up attacks on shipping before US vote, officials say
item.description:
By Parisa Hafezi, Jonathan Saul and Phil Stewart

DUBAI/LONDON/WASHINGTON, Oct 14 (Reuters) - Iran is deploying new tactics to target ships sailing through the Strait of Hormuz as it seeks to keep oil prices high and influence the US midterm elections, two senior Iranian officials told Reuters.

item.title: Saudi employee arrested for allegedly bugging OpenAI office
item.description:
A Saudi employee of OpenAI was arrested after allegedly planting a recording device in one of the company's San Francisco offices, the AI firm and federal prosecutors said Tuesday.

"We discovered a sophisticated recording device that was hidden inside one of our offices" and "referred the matter to the FBI," OpenAI told AFP in a statement.

OpenAI's security team found the device late last month and the employee, Saudi national Abdulrahman Alfozan, was arrested on October 9, the US Justice Department said.

item.title: Saudi Aramco administrative building attacked, limited fire reported
item.description:
By Timour Azhari and Menna AlaaElDin

RIYADH, Oct 13 (Reuters) - An administrative building belonging to Saudi Arabia's state-owned oil company Saudi Aramco in the eastern city of Dhahran was attacked, causing a limited fire, the Energy Ministry said in a statement on Wednesday as fighting between Yemen'sIran-allied Houthis and the kingdom intensified.

Authorities responded to the incident late on Tuesday and took necessary measures, the ministry said, adding that there were no injuries or deaths.
